📚 DAILY MARKET EDUCATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚖️ 1. POSITION SIZING: THE REAL EDGE IN FOREX
Position sizing is the calculation of how many units you should trade to risk a specific percentage of your account. Amateurs focus entirely on entry and exit points. Professionals know that size dictates survival.
- A correct stop loss with the wrong position size still destroys accounts
- Volatility changes by currency pair, requiring dynamic size adjustments
- Calculate your lot size before you even look at the trigger button
- Real Market Example: Risking 1 percent of a 10,000 dollar account on EUR/USD with a 50 pips stop loss requires a different lot size than risking that same amount on GBP/JPY with a 100 pips stop loss due to pip value differences.
PRO TIP: Never let a single trade dictate the health of your entire trading capital.

💧 2. LIQUIDITY AND SPREAD: THE HIDDEN COST OF TRADING
Liquidity refers to how easily a currency pair can be bought or sold without causing a drastic change in its price. The spread is the difference between the bid and ask price, widening when liquidity drops.
- Major pairs like EUR/USD offer deep liquidity and razor-thin spreads
- Crosses and exotic pairs have thinner liquidity and wider spreads
- High-impact news releases cause liquidity to vanish momentarily
- Real Market Example: During the Asian session, trading a cross pair like AUD/NZD often exposes you to wider spreads compared to the active London session overlap.
SMART MONEY RULE: Always factor the spread cost into your target and stop loss calculations before execution.

🎯 3. THREE DAILY TRADING TIPS
- Respect the London open: Volatility and volume surge between 0700 and 1000 GMT in major forex crosses, offering clean directional moves.
- Protect open profits: Move your stop loss to break even once the market reaches a one-to-one risk-to-reward ratio on USD pairs.
- Avoid low-liquidity traps: Skip trading major currencies during the late New York close and early Asian hours when ranges flatten out.

🛡️ 4. RISK MANAGEMENT: THE POWER OF TRUE DIVERSIFICATION
Diversification in forex is not just opening five different trades. It means trading uncorrelated currency pairs so a single market driver does not wipe out your entire portfolio.
- Buying EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and AUD/USD simultaneously is not diversified because they all correlate to US Dollar weakness
- True diversification involves pairing non-correlated economies
- Monitor your total exposure to a single base currency
- Real Market Example: Holding long positions in both EUR/USD and GBP/USD means you are doubling up on a short US Dollar thesis, effectively doubling your risk if USD bounces unexpectedly.
PRO TIP: Check currency correlation matrices weekly to ensure your open positions are genuinely independent of one another.
